headline: Over 24,000 students absent on first day of HSC exams
summary: Education Minister calls the high dropout rate a 'bad indicator' as 36% of regular students failed to fill out exam forms.
details: A total of 24,784 candidates were absent on the first day of the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations. Seven students were expelled for irregularities during the tests.
The number of absentees has risen steadily over the last three years. Last year, 19,759 students were absent on day one, while the previous year saw 15,203 absentees.

Alarmingly, 36% of regular students did not even fill out the exam forms. Out of approximately 1.5 million students who registered for Class 11 two years ago, only about 950,000 filled out forms for this year's exams.
The dropout rates vary by board: 44% in Madrasah boards, 54% in Technical boards, and 33% under general education boards.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haque Milon described this trend as a 'very bad indicator.' He suggested that a lack of proper classroom teaching and preparation may have led students to skip the exams.
The Minister noted that while a 10-15% dropout rate due to early marriage or family work was common, the current figures are significantly higher.
To address this crisis, the Ministry plans to place greater emphasis on teacher training to improve the quality of education and student preparation.
The exams are being held across 2,697 centers nationwide, with a total of 1,270,583 regular and irregular candidates eligible to participate.

headline_marked: Dhaka woman [[sentenced to death for butchering husband]] 5 years ago
headline: Dhaka woman sentenced to death for butchering husband 5 years ago
summary: Fatema Begum was convicted of killing her husband and dismembering his body into six pieces in Mohakhali, citing disputes over multiple marriages.
details: A Dhaka court has sentenced a woman, Fatema Begum (also known as Shilpi), to death for murdering her husband and dismembering his body into six pieces five years ago in Mohakhali.

The verdict was delivered on Thursday by Dhaka's 16th Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Nazmun Nahar Nipu. The court also sentenced her to seven years in prison for disposing of the body and fined her Tk 10,000.

The crime occurred on May 30, 2021, when Banani Police recovered a headless body from a drum in Amtali. Later that night, in the Mohakhali bus terminal area, police recovered severed arms and legs from a bag.
During investigation, Fatema confessed that tensions had risen due to family disputes, money, and her husband, Moyna Mia, having multiple marriages.

Police reports state that she fed her husband sleeping pills to leave him unconscious before slitting his throat. She then divided the body into six pieces and disposed of them in different locations, including Gulshan Lake.
The case was filed by the husband's second wife, Nasrin, on June 1, 2021. Following her arrest and confession, the trial began in March 2023 after the chargesheet was submitted in October 2022.
Despite claiming innocence during the trial, the court heard testimony from 17 of the 26 listed witnesses before delivering the final verdict.
